Declare the controls to derive from a table

Source: R/control_spec.R
control_spec.Rd

A control spec says what controls() permutes and plants: the column the negative control reassigns (on), the outcome the positive control plants an effect on (target), the planted effect per level of on in outcome-SD units (effect), the design strata within which on is permuted and the unit it is permuted at, the other unit-grained columns, the number of replicates and the seed. The spec is declared once, before any control table exists, and is the record of what was planted; print it to read the declaration.

Usage

control_spec(
  on = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  effect = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  grain = NULL,
  n = 1L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

on

The name of the column the negative control reassigns, by permuting it within strata at its unit. The outcome is not changed, so any real effect of on stays in it as unexplained variation. Must be a treatment or covariate column, categorical or whole-valued. NULL (the default) means the single treatment column of the table; a table with several or no treatment columns needs on named.

target

The name of one or more numeric outcome columns the positive control plants the effect on, or NULL for no positive control. A logical, factor, date, event or two-valued column is refused when the spec meets the table.

effect

The planted effect per level of on, in units of the target's standard deviation in the table at hand. That standard deviation includes the design variance and any real effect of on, so the size is not a multiple of an analysis's residual. Give it as a named numeric vector (c(G01 = 0.5, G02 = -0.5); a level not named shifts by zero), or list(sd = s) to draw one shift per level from a normal distribution with standard deviation s, under the spec's seed, when the spec first meets a table. Required with target. On a whole-valued target the shift is rounded, which can change the ratios between levels; shift_realised in @truth holds the effect that is in the table, and a warning (class masque_control_shape_rounded) marks a changed shape.

strata

Design columns within which on is permuted, or NULL for no stratification. Every unit of on must lie within one stratum. Prefer complete replicates to incomplete blocks; see controls().

unit

Design columns within which on is constant. on is then permuted across those units, so name the unit on was assigned at. NULL (the default) permutes rows, and in a plan picks the coarsest design column on which on is constant and which has enough units for a 5 percent level, with a warning (class masque_control_unit_ambiguous) when several qualify.

grain

A named list giving, for other analysed columns constant within a design unit, the unit columns: list(rain = "trial"). Such a column is permuted across its units in the null control, so it stays constant within each unit.

n

The number of negative (and positive) replicates.

seed

The seed of the control draws. Required.

Value

A masque_control_spec object, with a print method.

Details

The null control needs nothing beyond the seed. The negative control needs on, which defaults to the single treatment column of the table. The positive control needs target and effect together.

See also

controls(), control_table().

Examples

spec <- control_spec(
  on = "gen", target = "yield", effect = c(G01 = 0.5, G02 = -0.5),
  strata = "rep", n = 19L, seed = 2026L
)
spec
#> 
#> ── masque_control_spec ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Permuted column (on): gen
#> • Planted-effect target: yield
#> • Effect (target-SD units): G01 +0.5, G02 -0.5
#> • Strata: rep
#> • Unit of on: row
#> • Unit-grained columns: none declared
#> • Replicates: 19
#> • Seed: present
